events.title: Simon de Montfort's Parliament meets at Westminster
events.description: Ruling in the name of the captive Henry III, Simon de Montfort summoned knights from the shires and, for the first time, burgesses from the towns. It is seen as a forerunner of the House of Commons.
events.html: Ruling in the name of the captive Henry III, Simon de Montfort summoned knights from the shires and, for the first time, burgesses from the towns. It is seen as a forerunner of the House of Commons.

events.title: Trial of Charles I opens in Westminster Hall
events.description: A High Court of Justice set up by the Rump Parliament tried the King for treason against his people. Charles refused to recognise its authority and was beheaded ten days later.
events.html: A High Court of Justice set up by the Rump Parliament tried the King for treason against his people. Charles refused to recognise its authority and was beheaded ten days later.

events.title: Britain agrees preliminary peace with France and Spain
events.description: Preliminary articles signed at Versailles ended hostilities between Britain and the Bourbon powers. With peace with the United States already agreed, the war that won American independence was over.
events.html: Preliminary articles signed at Versailles ended hostilities between Britain and the Bourbon powers. With peace with the United States already agreed, the war that won American independence was over.

events.title: Convention of Chuenpi cedes Hong Kong Island to Britain
events.description: During the First Opium War, Charles Elliot and the Qing envoy Qishan agreed terms ceding Hong Kong Island. Neither government accepted the deal, but the 1842 Treaty of Nanking confirmed the cession.
events.html: During the First Opium War, Charles Elliot and the Qing envoy Qishan agreed terms ceding Hong Kong Island. Neither government accepted the deal, but the 1842 Treaty of Nanking confirmed the cession.

events.title: George V dies and Edward VIII becomes king
events.description: King George V died at Sandringham, and his eldest son succeeded as Edward VIII. Edward abdicated before the end of the year to marry Wallis Simpson, the only voluntary abdication in British history.
events.html: King George V died at Sandringham, and his eldest son succeeded as Edward VIII. Edward abdicated before the end of the year to marry Wallis Simpson, the only voluntary abdication in British history.

events.title: Nazi officials meet at Wannsee to coordinate the Holocaust
events.description: Chaired by Reinhard Heydrich, senior officials met at a villa on the Wannsee in Berlin to organise the 'Final Solution', the deportation and murder of Europe's Jews. The minutes survived the war.
events.html: Chaired by Reinhard Heydrich, senior officials met at a villa on the Wannsee in Berlin to organise the 'Final Solution', the deportation and murder of Europe's Jews. The minutes survived the war.

events.title: John F. Kennedy is inaugurated as US President
events.description: At 43, Kennedy became the youngest person elected President. His inaugural address urged Americans to 'ask what you can do for your country'. He was assassinated less than three years later.
events.html: At 43, Kennedy became the youngest person elected President. His inaugural address urged Americans to 'ask what you can do for your country'. He was assassinated less than three years later.

events.title: Iran releases 52 American hostages after 444 days
events.description: Minutes after Ronald Reagan was sworn in, Iran freed the Americans held since the seizure of the US embassy in Tehran in 1979. The crisis had overshadowed Jimmy Carter's final year in office.
events.html: Minutes after Ronald Reagan was sworn in, Iran freed the Americans held since the seizure of the US embassy in Tehran in 1979. The crisis had overshadowed Jimmy Carter's final year in office.

events.title: Barack Obama inaugurated as the first African American President
events.description: Before a crowd of some 1.8 million on the National Mall, Barack Obama was sworn in as the 44th President of the United States, taking office amid a deep financial crisis.
events.html: Before a crowd of some 1.8 million on the National Mall, Barack Obama was sworn in as the 44th President of the United States, taking office amid a deep financial crisis.
